summary: Build practical pipeline integrity, hydraulics, and maintenance skills in 5 days. Learn with real tools, standards, and exercises.
lede: Pipeline design, operation, and maintenance covers how teams assess flow, operating limits, and pipeline condition. For pipeline engineers, operations supervisors, integrity specialists, and maintenance planners, it develops practical skills in pressure-drop and wall-thickness checks, corrosion-threat assessment, and inspection and pigging plans. Learners also practice prioritizing maintenance, documenting defect decisions, and preparing integrity reports.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who work directly with pipeline design, operating control, inspection planning, and integrity support.
prerequisites: Participants should have working knowledge of oil and gas or industrial piping systems, basic engineering math, and familiarity with pipeline operations terminology. Prior exposure to pressure-flow concepts, corrosion basics, or maintenance planning is helpful, but advanced simulation or coding skills are not required. A laptop is recommended for calculation exercises and simulator-based demonstrations, depending on participant software access and institutional maturity.
